title: Skin layers & appendages anatomy
description: The five thick-skin epidermal strata, two dermal zones, hypodermis, receptors and follicle–gland units.

questions.question: What are the five epidermal layers in thick skin?
questions.answer: From deep to superficial they are stratum basale, spinosum, granulosum, lucidum and corneum. Thin skin does not have a distinct lucidum.

questions.question: Does the epidermis have its own blood vessels?
questions.answer: No. The epidermis receives nutrients by diffusion from capillaries in the underlying dermis.

questions.question: What is the stratum basale?
questions.answer: Deep single proliferative keratinocyte layer adjoining basement membrane. Function: Renews overlying epidermis.

questions.question: Where is the stratum granulosum located?
questions.answer: Flattened keratinocytes with keratohyalin granules and lipid-releasing lamellar bodies. Function: Builds the water-permeability barrier.

questions.question: What is the function of the stratum corneum?
questions.answer: Function: Principal external permeability barrier. Anucleate flattened corneocytes surrounded by intercellular lipid lamellae.
